t:
(a) In General.—Not later than 60 days after the end of each calendar year through 2020, the President shall submit to the committees of Congress specified in subsection (b) a report summarizing all licenses and other authorizations to export satellites and related items that are subject to the Export Administration Regulations (15 CFR part 730 et seq.) as a result of the enactment of section 1261(a). 
    (b) Committees of Congress Specified.—The committees of Congress specified in this subsection are—
        (1) the Committee on Foreign Relations, the Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, and the Select Committee on Intelligence of the Senate; and 
        (2) the Committee on Foreign Affairs and the Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence of the House of Representatives.

fable.w: The tempting reading is that a formal report on export licenses is a participatory process, or that the mention of licenses brings in outside parties. The report runs only from the President to congressional committees, all of which are inside the federal government. The licenses are just the subject of the report, and applications for licenses are not participation in any case. No state, tribe, expert, company or member of the public is consulted before a federal decision.
fable.s: the President shall submit to the committees of Congress specified in subsection (b) a report summarizing all licenses and other authorizations to export satellites and related items

opus.w: The only process here is a report from the President to congressional committees, which stays entirely inside the federal government. The export licenses described are things outside parties apply for, which is not participation in a decision. No state, expert, company or member of the public is consulted, and no hearing, comment period, advisory body or right to sue is created.
opus.s: the President shall submit to the committees of Congress specified in subsection (b) a report summarizing all licenses and other authorizations to export satellites and related items
opus.b: The tempting reading is that this counts as participation because it requires a formal report about export licenses. That fails because the report goes from the President to committees of Congress, and both sides are inside the federal government. The licenses mentioned are authorizations that outside parties apply for, and applications are not participation. No outside party is consulted before a decision.

qwen_chat.w: This section requires the President to submit a report to specific committees of Congress. According to the definition, Congress and its committees are inside the federal government, and reports to them do not constitute participation. There is no requirement for consultation with, or input from, any party outside the federal government.
qwen_chat.s: the President shall submit to the committees of Congress specified in subsection (b) a report summarizing all licenses and other authorizations to export satellites and related items
qwen_chat.b: Tempting-but-wrong reading: One might think that because the President is submitting a report, this involves some form of consultation or feedback loop with Congress. However, the definition explicitly states that reports to Congress are "inside the federal government" and do not constitute participation. The section only mandates a one-way report from the Executive branch to the Legislative branch, with no requirement for public comment, hearings, or consultation with outside entities.
